title: Compatibility of open star-shriek exchange with the actual derived scalar mates
statement:
Let $\lambda:A\to B$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For every scheme $T$, use $A_T=p_T^*A$, $B_T=p_T^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], their internal module categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and $T_T=B_T\otimes^L_{A_T}-$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Let $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ and $c:U\hookrightarrow X$ be quasi-compact open immersions, set $W=V\times_XU$, and let $a:W\hookrightarrow U$, $b:W\hookrightarrow V$ be the projections [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use exact extension by zero $b_!,c_!$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek]. Let $L$ be a finite-rank lisse $A_W$-module [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] and put $L_A=L$, $L_B=B_W\otimes_{A_W}L$.

For $R=A,B$, define $e_R:c_!Ra_{*,R}(L_R[0])\to Rj_{*,R}b_!(L_R[0])$ as the $c_!\dashv c^*$ adjunct of the inverse of the open-slice identification $c^*Rj_{*,R}b_!(L_R[0])\simeq Ra_{*,R}(L_R[0])$. Do not assume $e_R$ invertible. For any morphism $f$, define $\beta_{f,H}:T_{\mathrm{target}}Rf_{*,A}H\to Rf_{*,B}T_{\mathrm{source}}H$ as the $f_B^*\dashv Rf_{*,B}$ adjunct of the canonical scalar/pullback comparison followed by $T$ of the actual $A$-coefficient counit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Let $\delta_d:T_{\mathrm{target}}d_!\simeq d_!T_{\mathrm{source}}$ be the conjugate open-scalar isomorphism [def-sfb-derived-open-immersion-shriek-iso].

There is a canonical isomorphism $\iota:T_W(L[0])\simeq L_B[0]$ carrying the scalar unit to $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Put $\delta_{b,L}=b_!(\iota)\circ\delta_b$ and define $\Theta_a=(Ra_{*,B}\iota)\circ\beta_{a,L[0]}$ and $\Theta_j=(Rj_{*,B}\delta_{b,L})\circ\beta_{j,b_!L[0]}$. Then the following equality holds in the ordinary derived category of $B_X$-modules:
$$\Theta_j\circ T_X(e_A)=e_B\circ c_!(\Theta_a)\circ\delta_{c,Ra_{*,A}L[0]}.$$
Here both sides have source $T_Xc_!Ra_{*,A}L[0]$ and target $Rj_{*,B}b_!L_B[0]$. The equality uses the specified units and counits, rather than arbitrary isomorphisms of endpoints. No flatness of $\lambda$ is assumed. It includes $V=X$, $U=X$, $W=\varnothing$, and rank zero.

proof.text: Transport $L$ to the section-ring module category using [lem-sfb-internal-section-scalar-adjunction]. Its local trivializations are still finite free. Thus [lem-sfb-locally-free-derived-scalars] makes $L[0]$ K-flat and gives the canonical comparison $\iota:T_WL[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}(B_W\otimes_{A_W}L)[0]$. The first cited node identifies the specified scalar adjunctions, including their units, on K-flat representatives. Consequently the adjunct of this comparison is exactly $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and it transports back to the required internal-module isomorphism. No flatness of $B_W$ over $A_W$ is used.

proof.text: For $R=A,B$ and $M\in D(W,R)$ write $P_R(M)=Ra_{*,R}M$, $Q_R(M)=Rj_{*,R}b_!M$, and $u_{d,R}:1\xrightarrow{\sim}d_R^*d_{!,R}$ for the actual open unit. Let $E_{R,N}:c_R^*Rj_{*,R}N\to Ra_{*,R}b_R^*N$ be the actual exchange mate, and put $t_{R,M}=Ra_{*,R}(u_{b,R,M}^{-1})\circ E_{R,b_!M}$. This is the open-slice isomorphism used in the statement. Here is the normalization check: [lem-sfb-alpha-iso] identifies all pulled-back coefficient rings; [lem-sfb-module-direct-image-open-pasting](a) gives the ordinary restriction isomorphism, and [lem-sfb-proetale-open-restriction-counit] gives its actual counit equation. Apply [lem-sfb-kinjective-direct-image-open-word-model](i),(iii) to the words $c^*j_*$ and $a_*b^*$; every letter preserves K-injectives, so this isomorphism and its counit equation descend to the ordinary unbounded categories. The descended equation identifies it with the actual derived mate, by the derived adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. The invertible open units here are those specified in [lem-sfb-open-scalar-conjugate-normalization]. Thus $t_R$ is natural in $M$, and the definition of $e_R$ says exactly $c_R^*e_{R,M}\circ u_{c,R,P_R(M)}=t_{R,M}^{-1}$.

proof.text:
Write $\lambda_d:d_B^*T_{\mathrm{target}}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\mathrm{source}}d_A^*$ for the balanced scalar/pullback comparison, so its inverse is the $\theta_d$ in [lem-sfb-open-scalar-conjugate-normalization]. For every input $H$ that node states, for the specified conjugate $\delta_d$ rather than an arbitrary endpoint isomorphism,
$$u_{d,B,T H}^{-1}\circ d_B^*(\delta_{d,H})=T(u_{d,A,H}^{-1})\circ\lambda_{d,d_{!,A}H}.$$
Inverting this equality and composing with $u_{d,B,T H}$ gives
$$d_B^*(\delta_{d,H}^{-1})\circ u_{d,B,T H}=\lambda_{d,d_{!,A}H}^{-1}\circ T(u_{d,A,H}).$$
We will use the first equation for $b$ and the second for $c$. Both are identities on the entire unbounded category.

proof.text:
Set $M=L[0]$. Apply [lem-sfb-scalar-geometric-exchange-rectangle] to $(f,c,f',a)=(j,c,a,b)$ and input $b_!M$; its $\rho$ is our $\beta$ by the identical counit definition. It gives
$$Ra_{*,B}(\lambda_b)\circ E_B\circ c_B^*(\beta_{j,b_!M})=\beta_{a,b_A^*b_!M}\circ T_U(E_A)\circ\lambda_{c,Q_A(M)}.$$
By naturality of $E_B$, postcomposing with $Ra_{*,B}(u_{b,B,T_WM}^{-1})$ and inserting $c_B^*Rj_{*,B}(\delta_{b,M})$ on the left replaces $Ra_{*,B}(\lambda_b)$ by $Ra_{*,B}(T_Wu_{b,A,M}^{-1})$, using the first equation of step 3. Naturality of $\beta_a$ at $u_{b,A,M}^{-1}$ therefore gives
$$t_{B,T_WM}\circ c_B^*(Rj_{*,B}(\delta_{b,M})\circ\beta_{j,b_!M})=\beta_{a,M}\circ T_U(t_{A,M})\circ\lambda_{c,Q_A(M)}.$$
Now postcompose with $Ra_{*,B}(\iota)$ and use naturality of $t_B$ at $\iota$. In the notation of the item this is
$$t_{B,L_B[0]}\circ c_B^*(\Theta_j)=\Theta_a\circ T_U(t_{A,M})\circ\lambda_{c,Q_A(M)}.$$
These substitutions use only functoriality, the two displayed naturality squares, and the cited normalized rectangle; no comparison map $\beta$ has been inverted.

proof.text:
Put $P=P_A(M)$, $Q=Q_A(M)$, $\tau=t_{A,M}$ and $\tau'=t_{B,L_B[0]}$. Precompose both proposed arrows with $\delta_{c,P}^{-1}$, obtaining arrows with source $c_{!,B}T_UP$. Apply the bijection $h\mapsto c_B^*h\circ u_{c,B,T_UP}$ of $c_{!,B}\dashv c_B^*$. The transpose of the left side is
$$c_B^*(\Theta_j)\circ c_B^*T_X(e_{A,M})\circ c_B^*(\delta_{c,P}^{-1})\circ u_{c,B,T_UP}
=c_B^*(\Theta_j)\circ\lambda_{c,Q}^{-1}\circ T_U(c_A^*e_{A,M}\circ u_{c,A,P})
=(\tau')^{-1}\circ\Theta_a\circ T_U(\tau)\circ T_U(\tau^{-1})
=(\tau')^{-1}\circ\Theta_a.$$
The first equality uses step 3 and naturality of $\lambda_c$ at $e_A$; the second uses step 4 and the defining adjunct equation in step 2. The transpose of the right side, after cancellation of $\delta_c$, is
$$c_B^*(e_{B,L_B[0]})\circ c_B^*c_{!,B}(\Theta_a)\circ u_{c,B,T_UP}
=c_B^*(e_{B,L_B[0]})\circ u_{c,B,P_B(L_B[0])}\circ\Theta_a
=(\tau')^{-1}\circ\Theta_a.$$
Here the first equality is naturality of the actual open unit. The transposes agree, so the Hom-bijection and then the isomorphism $\delta_c$ give exactly the required equality.

proof.text: All formulas are identities of natural transformations on the ordinary unbounded categories and were specialized only at $M=L[0]$ and the normalized $\iota$. For $V=X$ or $U=X$ the relevant identity-open comparisons give the same equations with identities. For $W=\varnothing$ or local rank zero the inputs and their images are zero and the equations remain valid. At no point was $e_R$, $\beta_a$, or $\beta_j$ inverted, or a flatness condition on the coefficient map imposed.
